entry.title: How to evolve superstars in WWE 2K25
entry.summary:
WWE 2K25's MyFaction mode can be highly grindy if you don't have cards of higher rarities, but the ability to evolve some of your existing items will certainly help you in the process.
While the evolution method is exclusive to the MyFaction mode, it can benefit all game modes. The cards that you evolve could end up helping you unlock wrestlers and more that can become useable in the general roster. This guide will help you to understand how evolution works and which cards can be improved over time.
WWE 2K25 Superstar Evolutions explained
Every wrestler card in MyFaction belongs to a certain rarity, starting from Bronze. The lower the rarity, the weaker its stats are. Cards that can evolve will improve their rarity and in-game stats. It's easy to identify cards that can evolve, as they have DNA symbols on their left side.
If you check out the screenshot below, you'll notice that specific tasks are shown on my screen. Once you complete all three tasks, your card will evolve to the next tier (Sapphire, in the case of Bronson Reed).
Image via Destructoid
The number of tasks that you have to complete can also vary. Usually, cards can evolve by only one tier, but it's still handy for improving your Faction. Getting higher-tier cards at the start of your MyFaction adventures is hard, so having a card that can upgrade by at least one rarity will be helpful.
For starters, we all receive two cards that can be upgraded. One will belong to men's wrestling, while the other will be from women's wrestling. I am sure we will be getting plenty more upgradeable cards in the future, as some are also available in the packs.
Certain wrestlers also have Persona cards available in the game, and you can get them to unlock alternative appearances for your superstars. Make sure to check this guide out to learn more about how to get all the available Persona cards in WWE 2K25.

entry.title: How to find 3 Golden Llamas in Fortnite
entry.summary:
Have you ever encountered a Golden Llama in Fortnite's modes? Although regular llamas occasionally appear as rare loot sources, golden versions are almost unheard of except during various events. Considering Chapter 6, Season 2 is all about gold, this one feels particularly fitting.
How to find Golden Llamas in Fortnite Chapter 6, Season 2
Golden Llamas are rare loot containers that spawn randomly around Fortnite's map. Since they have random spawns, there's no one specific location to camp if you're wishing to find them as part of a weekly quest or event. Instead, your goal is to survive as long as possible and move around the map in hopes of spotting one of these in the wild.
Screenshot by Destructoid
Golden Llamas appear as a goofy-looking gold llama that's slightly smaller than the player's model. If you're familiar with the game's rainbow versions from previous seasons, they look almost the exact same with a distinct color change.
Since Golden Llamas can spawn anywhere, there's a chance you'll encounter them in strange spots like the sides of cliffs, near the edge of the map, or on top of massive mountains. I even found one of a cliff's edge that I could barely navigate, making it a little tricky to search it for loot. Sometimes, it requires a bit of trial and error.
If you're focused on completing your quests and don't mind risking a loss or two, you can start gliding from the Battle Bus immediately after jumping out to help you search for Golden Llamas from a bird's-eye view. Although you won't reach the ground as quickly, you might get lucky and spot one from the skies, letting you drop to its exact spot and claim it before someone else accidentally stumbles upon it. Otherwise, you can just play your matches normally and hope you find one by chance.

entry.title: R.E.P.O Energy Crystals: All uses and how to get
entry.summary:
Wondering how to use Energy Crystals in R.E.P.O? As you complete your first few runs in R.E.P.O, you'll encounter a shop where you can buy upgrades, weapons, and more. If you're wondering what Energy Crystals are and if they're worth your time, see the full explainer below.
What are Energy Crystals used for in R.E.P.O?
Image by Destructoid
Energy Crystals are used to recharge almost all weapons in the game, including non-electric things like the baseball bat and inflatable hammer.
You can buy these from within the shop in between levels/ They are yellow in color and usually priced anywhere between $7k to $14k.
When equipping a weapon, you’ll see a white bar beneath its icon at the bottom of the screen. This tells you how much charge the item has available. Once all the bars are gone, the item cannot be used again until recharged with an Energy Crystal.
How to use Energy Crystals in R.E.P.O
Image by Destructoid
Luckily, it's a simple process to use Energy Crystals in R.E.P.O. Simply buy a Crystal from the shop, like any other item or upgrade. Once you return to your ship, you will find a crystal station on the right side. Here, you can pick up weapons and drop them in the little bin to the left of the machine. This will charge the weapon up and it is ready for use again.
Energy Crystals have a limited supply and will break once depleted. You’ll need to buy more, therefore, to keep recharging your weapons. Although it may be tempting to spend all your money on mines and grenades, it's a far better investment to save up for a powerful weapon and buy Energy Crystals to keep it charged.
Now you should be all set to use Energy Crystals and keep your weapons in working order. For more R.E.P.O tips and tricks, see our guide to finding a game group to play with.

entry.title: How to find Pump and Dump in Fortnite
entry.summary:
Fortnite Chapter 6, Season 2 has numerous peculiar weapons, from the Sub-Zero Combat Kit to Big Dill's favorite, the Pump & Dump. Acting as both a shotgun and SMG, the Pump & Dump gives you a two-in-one special at the cost of using a bunch of ammo.
Where to find Pump and Dump in Fortnite
You can find the Pump & Dump shotgun-SMG-mix as chest loot, floor spawns, and player elimination drops during your Fortnite matches. At any point during your match, you can find this gun — usually as a rare-grade drop — like you would any other weapon.
Screenshot by Destructoid
Although the rarity of the Pump & Dump weapon varies, you'll usually find it as a rare-tier gun glowing blue. This makes it relatively common compared to epic, legendary, and Mythic-grade variants, but you won't necessarily see it everywhere. However, I tend to have much better luck finding this in Ranked mode than unranked, so it's worth a quick swap if you've yet to encounter this weapon.
How to find a Mythic Pump and Dump in Fortnite
Screenshot by Destructoid
Alongside regular chest and floor drops, you can find a Mythic-grade Pump & Dump weapon at the Crime City Black Market for one Dill Bit. Upon running in and approaching the spot Skillet hovers around, you'll spot a display case containing the Mythic Pump & Dump to buy at any point during your match. This one is, unsurprisingly, much more powerful than its rare-tier counterpart but is far more challenging to obtain.
Since you need Dill Bits, you'll have to break into one of Fletcher Kane's vaults or armored vehicles to claim some of these coins before venturing to Crime City's Black Market and claiming the item. There's a high chance you'll find other players along the way, so watch your surroundings in case someone tries to initiate an unexpected fight.

How GTA 6 will eventually look on our consoles (and PC) is still a matter of great intrigue, but a clip made in Fortnite is trying to show us a glimpse of the possible future.
In a clip uploaded by YouTuber Brux, we managed to get an extremely GTA-fashioned action scene made using Fortnite's in-game engine. It's a known fact that Epic allows many tools for modders to create their own maps, and some of them are extremely popular.
While the creation shown in the clip might not be functional, it couldn't have appeared at a better time as we await the next chapter of GTA.
Viral GTA 6 clip shows the real potential of Fortnite's engine
Many social media users were left confused when this short clip from Blux surfaced online. It wouldn't be the first time that GTA 6's clips have surfaced online (who can forget the infamous leaks), but this one comes to us thanks to Fortnite. According to the creator, it took them nine months to create.
In the clip, we can see a female character hijacking a car before being chased by the police. As a shootout ensues, it becomes quite clear that the footage is definitely from Fortnite. We have the classic instance of the blue shield being chipped away as the officer got shot and glimpses of the game's building creation.
Despite some accounts on X spreading false rumors about it, the creator has made clear how the clip was made on the 2018 engine and how long it took.
I won't rule out seeing more clips until we get a confirmation from Rockstar about when GTA 6 will go live. Based on the current information, the game is expected to be released in 2025 and will be available on current-gen consoles. A PC release or its potential timeline has yet to be announced, as the gaming community eagerly waits for Rockstar's next major showcase.

Plus with EPYC Turin supporting the new AMD P-State CPU frequency scaling driver there is greater headroom in optimizing for power efficiency if so desired. entry.title: Monster Hunter needs a full-scale rebirth, but its contradictions are fascinating
entry.summary:
Monster Hunter Wilds is the fastest-selling game in Capcom's history. It continues to lord over the Steam charts, with peaks that might cause Counter-Strike 2 to glance momentarily down from its Olympus of user-created hats, and while people are still booting the dung out of the PC version's performance, verdicts upon the beast-punching as a whole are glowing.
To suggest that now is the time to go back to formula is probably pure contrarianism, but Wilds makes my brain itch. Building on (and hopefully not just recapping) Brendy's excellently ambivalent Monster Hunter Wilds review, I think the series is balancing on the edges of contradictions that extend throughout its design, from the combat through the user interface to the world and narrative themes. I think it's been doing that for years, in fact, but Wilds, for me, is where Monster Hunter's confusion about itself has come to a head.

entry.title: RPS Verdict: Monster Hunter Wilds
entry.summary:
Is it wrong to eat a dinosaur that wants to be eaten? What if it asks you to make a little hat out of its gall bladder? What if the gall bladder has different opinions on the matter? Discover the answers to these and more as our merry band of conservation enthusiasts/trophy hunters discuss Monster Hunter Wilds! Nic: Life, the absolute bastard, has kept me away from the Monst. Let me experience it through you. What's the best Monst so far? Brendan: I am fond of the squiddy critters that slop about. The Nu Udra is a giant gloopy octopus that feels like a stand-out fight partly because of its many, many arms, but also because of the environment you fight it in. It's horrible (in a fun way) to wade about in the oil of this region, and try to avoid the flames that inevitably start to spread. Another later squid-like beast has some horrible knifey hands at the end of its tentacles, but I'll let the readers discover the rest of that creep's tactics by themselves. Ollie: I'm partial to the Yian Kut-Ku myself. It was the very first monster I ever fought in any Monster Hunter, back in the days of Monster Hunter Freedom on my PSP. And all these years later, I still recognised all its moves, and it made the whole act of beating up the big fire-breathing chicken even more enjoyable and satisfying than it already was.

entry.title: The Gothic Remake demo reveals an RPG powered by wheeling, dealing, and growling
entry.summary:
I’ve never played 2001’s Gothic, developed by Piranha Bytes, but Sin has an article from 2016 about why it is “more believable than modern RPGs”. In that piece, she paints an absorbing picture of a magically quarantined penal colony, where three factions of prisoners enjoy an uneasy truce. In this crammed ocean vent of a setting, fights generally end in defeat rather than death, reputation isn’t just a points gauge, and the player character’s centrality is an accident. It sounds pretty thrilling.
I am still searching for this RPG in the Steam prologue demo for Alkimia Interactive’s Gothic reboot. There are certainly some intrigues afoot, and I’m quite enjoying the desolate quarry scenery, but I’m distracted by aspects of the presentation, not least the fact that the prologue character looks like a Funko Pop incarnation of Highlander’s Christopher Lambert.

entry.title: Sid Meier's Civilization VII review
entry.summary:
Civilization is one of only two games I’ve had on every computer I’ve ever owned, in its multiple versions, since I first encountered it. (The other is NetHack.) It’s also important in my family. My wife plays it frequently (although she’s been on a Balatro kick recently), and I remember my middle child, in middle school, responding to a vocabulary quiz where they were asked to define “civilization” with the answer: “Civilization is a game designed by Sid Meier.”
Obviously, I’m well disposed toward this long-running turn-based strategy series. But Civilization 7, as currently constituted, has some real flaws – and though I expect they may be fixed in future updates (and there are workarounds), some of this is a little sloppy.
The most basic issue is: combat sucks.

entry.title: Na trhu chybí tisíce odborníků na čipy. FEKT VUT proto otevře nový studijní program, který v Česku nemá obdoby
entry.summary: Okolo tří tisíc odborníků v Česku a až padesát tisíc specialistů v rámci Evropy. Taková je přibližně podle Viléma Kledrowetze z Ústavu mikroelektroniky FEKT VUT stávající poptávka po lidech v oblasti čipů a moderních polovodičů. I proto letos v září na fakultě otevřou ojedinělý bakalářský a magisterský program, který bude právě na tuto oblast zaměřen. Propojí teorii s praxí, nabídne zkušenosti odborníků z jiných fakult a z průmyslu i množství zajímavých stáží v Česku a ve světě.

entry.title: A bolt of lightning, a shocking experience
entry.summary: God of Thunder, the Zelda-esque game, is now ready for public testing! Prepare yourself to take on the role of Thor, the god of thunder, as he battles his way through the three part game, facing enemies and challenging environmental puzzles, all to finally face down challenging end bosses, culminating in Loki himself. The implementation in ScummVM is slightly different from the original, in that whilst it has a high score table like the original, you don't have to go through the steps of creating an account and being limited to only a single savegame. Also, unfortunately, the game uses a special music format that will need to be implemented from scratch by someone with experience. So for now, no music playback will occur, though in-game sound effects play back fine. To participate in the testing, ensure you have a daily development build. The game itself is freeware, and can be downloaded from the Adept Software website. We encourage all players to submit feedback and bug reports through our issue tracker.And please take some screenshots along the way. Have you the skill to defeat Loki, or will you be defeated by the cunning enemies, or be stymied figuring out the puzzles. Play, and find out. >
